title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Santorini and eating with it

steps.title: Labels and Vinsanto
steps.body: Labels show Santorini PDO, the producer and sometimes Nykteri or a single vineyard. Vinsanto, Santorini's sweet wine, is made from at least 51% Assyrtiko with Aidani, from grapes sun-dried for about 12 to 14 days, then fermented and aged at least two years in oak, often much longer. It's amber, with raisin, apricot, coffee and spice, balanced by acidity.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Dry Assyrtiko suits Greek seafood: grilled octopus, sea bass, squid, shellfish, and local dishes like fava, a yellow split pea purée, tomatokeftedes, tomato fritters, and feta. Its acidity cuts through olive oil. Vinsanto suits dried fruit, nuts, blue cheese and chocolate. Serve Assyrtiko at 8 to 11 degrees.

options: From sun-dried grapes, aged in oak

steps.body: Top Santorini Assyrtiko ages well for 10 to 15 years, gaining smoky, honeyed notes while keeping its acidity.

steps.prompt: Dry Assyrtiko is a good match for grilled octopus.
steps.explanation: Yes. Its acidity and saltiness suit grilled seafood.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show Santorini PDO and sometimes Nykteri
Assyrtiko suits octopus, fava and feta
